notes: Pencil, four figures at the extreme treble edge, their tops shaved by the paper edge: [4 or 7] 9 2 4, i.e. 4.9.24 or 7.9.24. The first figure carries a crossbar over a descending stem, which in these hands can be either an open-topped 4 or a crossed 7, so I have left date_iso at the month. e2 carries the roll number 1263 in a smaller hand, clear of the edge; e3 shows the printed leader label WELTE-MIGNON No. 1263, Minuett G major, Paderewski; e4 blank.
Nothing written. e1 is the leader tab with the colour target, e2 the cloth-to-paper joint, e3 plain paper with a single ink speck.

No handwriting. Buff paper. e1 carries a printed legal notice of eight or nine lines set across the roll (a manufacturer's and patent notice, too blurred at this resolution to transcribe, and printed rather than written); e2 has only an ink blot; e3 is the tail with its red cloth.

Pencil, five figures run together at the treble edge, steeply slanted: [8?] 1 1 2 2, i.e. 8.11.22. The month and year are plain; the first figure is two strokes converging on a single bottom bowl with the upper loop left open, the form reading.md warns is an 8 taken for a 6, so the day is either 8 or 6 and I have left date_iso at the month. e2 carries the roll number 1307 in a neater hand, which agrees with the leader label in e4 (WELTE-MIGNON No. 1307, An den Fruehling, Op. 43 No. 1, E. Grieg); e3 shows only ink offsets around the perforations.

Nothing written. e1 and e3 are plain red paper with a few specks, e2 the cloth leader joint; e4 shows the printed leader labels only (WELTE-MIGNON No. 1339, Traviata, with the English care notice), which are printed rather than written.

Nothing written. e1 and e3 show the cloth leader with its printed labels (WELTE-MIGNON No. 1343, Romeo and Juliette, Potpourri, Ch. Gounod, with a printed facsimile signature and the English care notice); e2 is plain red paper with a torn edge.

One pencil group of five figures at the treble edge of e2, plainly legible as 2 8 4 9 2 (the third figure is the open-topped German 4, possibly a 7). Read as a date it would give 28.4.92, which cannot be a workshop date, so I take it for a number and have left reading and date_iso empty rather than force it. The other crops carry only the master's ruled pencil lines and perforations.

Pencil group of five figures at the treble edge of e1, steeply slanted: the first three are plainly 1 1 5, the last two are each a bowl with a descending stroke. Read straight off, 11.5.99, which cannot be a workshop date; if the fourth figure is a 0 rather than a 9 it would give 11.5.09, but I cannot see that, so I have left the date empty. Worth a second reader. e2 carries the roll number in a neater hand, 1 3 5 7 (the last figure a crossed 7 with a long tail), agreeing with the printed leader label in e4 (WELTE-MIGNON No. 1357, Pas des Echarpes, 3eme Air de Ballet Op. 37, C. Chaminade); e3 has only perforations and a small stain.

e1 carries a large pencil autograph across the width of the roll, two lines with a long flourish under them: a capital-F surname that I read as Foster (Faster is possible) preceded by a small a, then June, 1910. English wording and an English-looking hand, so it looks like an artist's signature and date rather than a workshop punch mark, and I have left reading and date_iso empty; the team may still want the June 1910 as a terminus. Nothing on e2 to e5 but perforations and a crease.

e1 carries a rubber stamp set diagonally across the paper, not writing: a heavy blotted mark with a tail, then a point, then four figures 4 1 [2 or 3] 8. The leading mark is the fixed blob reading.md warns about, so I have not counted it as a digit; the figures alone give 4.1.28. The third figure is clogged with ink and could as well be a 3, which would make it 4.1.38, so the year is the weak point. e4 carries the roll number 1443 in pencil, agreeing with the printed leader label in e5 (WELTE-MIGNON No. 1443, Sonata Appassionata Op. 57, 2nd and 3rd movements, Beethoven); e2, e3 and e6 are blank.

Nothing written by hand. e1 is plain paper with perforations, e2 a printed notice block (M. Welte & Sons, Inc.), e3 a pasted photographic artist label printed Famous Artists are reproduced on THE WELTE-MIGNON, 273 Fifth Ave. N.Y.C. with a portrait and a printed facsimile signature, e4 the cloth leader joint.
Nothing written. The paper is ruled all over with the master's fine pencil lines, which is what shows on every crop; e1, e4 and e5 carry small graphite smudges over those lines, none of them figures.

e2 shows 26. 1. 76 in pencil, plainly legible, but on the olive repair paper spliced to the head of the roll and in a later hand, so 26 January 1976 and a repairer's note rather than a workshop punch date; I have left reading and date_iso empty. e1 is the scanner's colour target, e3 a printed notice showing through from the other side of the paper.

Nothing written. Olive-grey paper; e1 shows a printed notice block showing through from the other side, too faint to transcribe, e2 the pinked joint between the paper and the red cloth leader, e3 the scanner's colour target.
